plan:
# Details panel session: Fired Title

## Pitch

**Lens grinder:** "Kiln Window." The panel is 280px wide and shows only the title, its preview and Save. My strange part is that the preview shows the title through the card's own clip, at the card's real width. You see the raw draft and the finished card side by side. Rows: card, narrow panel, title field, fit preview, save, close.

**Kinetic sculptor:** "Three Firings." The title has three states: Draft, Checked and Saved. Each state has one square glyph drawn at the stroke weight of 15px text. Hollow means draft, half means checked, filled means saved. Cut everything else. Rows: card trigger, panel, field with stage glyph, save, close guard. Five rows, maybe six.

**Game interface designer:** "Glaze Settles." The panel slides in for 180ms and stops. On save, a single sheen crosses the title once and ends. Each motion has a reason to stop, and nothing loops. The feeling I want to protect: closing should never cost the visitor a sentence they typed. Rows: card, panel, field, save with sheen, close guard, keyboard hint strip.

**Floating market clerk:** "Ledger Panel." Counts sit in one aligned column: characters, lines on the card, version number. Below that is a revision list where every saved title keeps its time and length in tabular figures. The material is the title text, so show what it was and what it is now. Rows: card, panel, field, count column, save, revision ledger.

## Clash

**Lens grinder:** Counterexample. "Migrate billing exports to the new warehouse schema" saves fine and then gets clipped to "Migrate billing exports to the new…" on the card. A glyph that says Saved is wrong about what the teammate will see.
**Kinetic sculptor:** Then the fit preview earns a row. The keyboard hint strip does not. Every shortcut belongs in a control's accessible name and visible label.
**Game interface designer:** Fine. The sheen still has a reason. It marks the moment the title becomes fired.
**Floating market clerk:** Before we vote on motion, Kinetic sculptor, you have said least about the panel. Try closing it with Escape mid-edit and tell us what happens.
**Kinetic sculptor:** In the current sketch my draft is gone and focus lands on the page body. That is the unresolved point. Who owns the dirty close?
**Game interface designer:** I demoed it with the sheen on and with the sheen off. The filled glyph plus "Saved 14:06" read the same in both, and the sheen pulled my eye off the close guard. I drop the sheen. The guard gets the row.
**Floating market clerk:** Then my revision ledger is a seventh job inside a one-title edit. I'll cut it. Keep the version number, because Save needs it to detect a teammate's rename.
**Lens grinder:** Agreed, but the preview needs a phone width. Otherwise it only tells the truth on desktop.

## Decision

The team selects a project-tool details panel in which a visitor opens a card by keyboard, edits its title against a live card-width preview, saves it with honest pending, failure and conflict states, and closes without losing a draft while focus returns to the same card.

Concept: Fired Title

The craft reading comes from the Australian Museum's account of Egyptian faience (https://australian.museum/learn/cultures/international-collection/ancient-egyptian/egyptian-faience/). In that account, a shaped body only becomes its finished surface after drying and firing. The pack maps this onto text states only: Draft, Checked and Saved. The forms are plain squares. The pack uses no symbols, motifs or claims of cultural authenticity.

Contributions:
- Lens grinder: the card fit preview, plus its 180px phone width.
- Kinetic sculptor: the three-glyph stage rule at text weight. Also the cut of the hint strip, and pressing the open question of who owns a dirty close until the team answered it.
- Game interface designer: the 180ms slide that stops. After the demo, they withdrew the save sheen.
- Floating market clerk: tabular count alignment, and the version check behind conflict detection.

Rejected direction: the clerk's Ledger Panel. A revision list adds a second data job to a single-title edit. Its useful part, the version number, moved into row 5.

No component_source was supplied. Two idea bank entries shaped the mechanisms:
- The riffle label button became row 5. It keeps reserved label width and the swap from action to completion. It adds pending, failure and conflict states, and drops the housing decoration.
- The bottom sheet became row 2. It keeps Escape, a Close button and focus return. It drops drag and snap points, and returns focus by card id.

Six rows earn their place because each owns one failure the task can produce:
1. The card cannot be reached by keyboard.
2. The panel traps focus or loses it.
3. The draft and the saved title drift apart without notice.
4. The saved title clips on the card.
5. A save fails or overwrites a teammate.
6. Closing drops typed text.

A seventh row would duplicate one of these.

## Build notes

1. Route Escape, Close, and opening another card through one `requestClose(reason)` function that checks `draft.stage !== 'saved'` before calling `dialog.close()`. Call `preventDefault` on the dialog `cancel` event so Escape cannot bypass the gate.
2. Look up the return target with `document.querySelector('[data-card-id="c-3"]')` after the save re-sort, never with a stored element reference. Test it by saving a title that moves the card from position 1 to position 5.
3. The row 4 measuring card must share the `.card-title` class and token font with row 1. Run the binary search inside `requestAnimationFrame`, and announce in the live region only when the result changes between "fits" and "clipped".

close-blocked: held open while row 6 shows, reached by Escape or Close with a dirty draft
narrow: full width under 640px with 16px padding
reduced-motion: appears without slide
focus: 2px ring on Close

components.name: Title draft field
components.description: Labelled title input with a stage glyph and word for Draft, Checked or Saved, a tabular count and a revert action.
components.purpose: Edit the title and always show whether the text on screen is draft, checked or saved.
components.use: A lead types a long title and reads 'Checked · 52 / 80' before saving.
components.input: Type in the field by keyboard or on-screen keyboard. Click, tap or press Enter on Revert to saved, which appears when the draft is dirty.
components.outcome: The stage moves to Checked 600ms after the last keystroke when the trimmed title is 1 to 80 characters and differs from saved. Row 5 sets Saved.
components.recovery: Revert to saved restores the saved title and the Saved stage. Native Ctrl+Z works in the field.
components.mechanism: The draft is stored per card id in the shared store. Validation trims whitespace. Glyphs are 10px squares at a 1.5px stroke to match 15px text: hollow for Draft, half-filled for Checked, filled for Saved. Each glyph pairs with its word. The draft has a 1px dashed underline, and the saved title has none. The count uses tabular-nums in a 7ch slot.
components.nearestAnalogue: 2026-10-30 link options field flagged drift between the screen and the clipboard. This field flags drift between the draft and the saved title.
components.usefulness: Visitors often close panels believing a typed title saved itself.
components.creativeDifference: Text moves through raw, checked and finished stages, each with its own shape.
states: saved: filled square, reached on open and after save
draft: hollow square and dashed underline, reached on typing
checked: half square, reached 600ms after a valid edit
empty: 'Title needed', reached when trimmed text is empty
over-limit: count reads '84 / 80' with 'Shorten by 4'
unchanged: 'Same as saved', reached when the draft equals saved
focus: 2px ring

components.name: Card fit preview
components.description: Live render of the draft title inside the card's real width and two-line clamp, reporting fit or the last visible word.
components.purpose: Show how the title will read on the board before it is saved.
components.use: A lead sees 'Clipped after "new" at phone width' and shortens the title.
components.input: Display follows the field. Choose Desktop 232px or Phone 180px with a two-option radio group. Keyboard: Tab into the group, arrow keys select.
components.outcome: The preview reads 'Fits in 2 lines' or 'Clipped after "new"' at the chosen width.
components.recovery: Editing the field updates the preview on the next frame. Switching width never changes the draft.
components.mechanism: A hidden measuring card uses the same CSS class as row 1, at the chosen width. Overflow is detected by comparing scrollHeight with two line-heights. The cut word is found by binary search over the word count. The live region announces only when the fit state changes.
components.nearestAnalogue: None in recent dates. 2026-10-30 reserved skeleton matched loaded geometry, but it held layout and did not measure text.
components.usefulness: A title that saves fine but clips on the card hides its key word from teammates.
components.creativeDifference: The preview is a staged view of the finished card, made from the same rule that renders it.
states: fits: 'Fits in 2 lines', reached when text fits
clipped: ellipsis with the last visible word named
phone: 180px measurement, reached by the Phone radio
empty: preview shows 'Untitled' in muted text
focus: 2px ring on the radio group

components.name: Save title button
components.description: Native submit button with a reserved-width label covering idle, saving, saved, failed and conflict outcomes.
components.purpose: Commit a checked title and state exactly what happened.
components.use: A lead saves, and a teammate's earlier rename surfaces as 'Renamed by Ana 14:05'.
components.input: Click or tap Save. Keyboard: Enter in the field, Ctrl+Enter or Cmd+Enter anywhere in the panel, or Tab to the button and press Space.
components.outcome: The label swaps Save, Saving, then 'Saved 14:06'. The card title updates and row 3 shows Saved.
components.recovery: On failure, the label reads 'Not saved · Retry' and the draft is kept. On conflict, two buttons appear: Use mine and Keep theirs. Presses while saving are ignored.
components.mechanism: The form submit handler compares the stored version with the baseline captured at open. A local store resolves after 700ms. Demo toggles force a failure or a conflict. The label width is reserved for 'Not saved · Retry'. The button is disabled unless the stage is Checked.
components.nearestAnalogue: 2026-10-30 copy link button and 2026-10-30 retry guard. Those copied or refetched. This save writes user text and detects a teammate's overwrite.
components.usefulness: Silent overwrites and lost failures are the two save errors that cost work.
components.creativeDifference: The saved state is the finished surface. The button only accepts text that has passed the checked stage.
states: disabled: stage is Draft or invalid
idle: 'Save', reached at Checked
saving: disabled 'Saving'
saved: 'Saved 14:06'
failed: 'Not saved · Retry', reached by demo toggle
conflict: Use mine and Keep theirs, reached by version mismatch
focus: 2px ring

components.name: Unsaved close guard
components.description: Inline alert in the panel footer that intercepts a dirty close with three choices, with Keep editing focused first.
components.purpose: Stop a close from dropping typed text, and let the visitor choose.
components.use: A lead presses Escape mid-edit and reads 'Unsaved title · "Migrate billing exports"'.
components.input: Click or tap Save and close, Discard or Keep editing. Keyboard: focus lands on Keep editing. Tab and Shift+Tab move between the three, Enter or Space activates, and Escape again means Keep editing.
components.outcome: Save and close runs row 5, then closes. Discard closes and keeps the draft in a one-slot buffer. Keep editing returns focus to the field with the caret at the end.
components.recovery: Reopening the same card in the session offers 'Restore discarded draft'. If Save and close fails, the panel stays open with row 5's failure state.
components.mechanism: Triggered from the dialog cancel event, the Close button and row 1 opening another card. The alert uses role=alert and is inline, so no second dialog stacks. The discard buffer holds one draft per session.
components.nearestAnalogue: None direct. 2026-10-30 copy repair notice kept a failure visible until fixed. This guard prevents the loss before it happens.
components.usefulness: An Escape press that silently discards a sentence breaks trust in the panel.
components.creativeDifference: The safest choice gets focus first, and Escape can never discard.
states: hidden: draft clean
shown: three choices with the draft quoted, reached by a dirty close
saving: Save and close disabled while row 5 runs
discarded: panel closed, buffer filled
restorable: 'Restore discarded draft' on reopen
focus: 2px ring on each choice

demo.sharedState: One store holds six cards (id, title, version), openId, a per-card draft {text, stage}, the baselineVersion captured on open, and a one-slot discard buffer. Row 1 opens row 2 for card c-3 'Billing export' v4. Row 3 writes the draft, and row 4 measures it. Row 5 saves when the stage is Checked and bumps the version. A demo toggle sets c-3 to v5 'Billing exports' by Ana to force a conflict. Row 6 gates every close. On close, row 2 returns focus to row 1 by id after the alphabetical re-sort.
